question: The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea was written in the:
solution:
The correct answer is __**1st century AD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Periplus of the Erythraean Sea** is a Greco-Roman navigational text written in the **1st century AD**.
 
• It provides detailed information about trade routes, ports, and commodities traded across the **Red Sea, Arabian Sea, and Indian Ocean**.
 
• The text is believed to have been authored by an anonymous Greek merchant or sailor.
 
• It serves as a crucial historical source for understanding maritime trade and cultural exchanges between the Roman Empire, India, East Africa, and Arabian regions.
 
• The document mentions **Muziris**, an important port on the southwestern coast of India, highlighting India's significance in ancient trade networks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periplus:**

 
 
• A "Periplus" is a type of navigational text used by ancient sailors and traders to describe coastlines, ports, and trade routes.
 
• The term is derived from the Greek word "periplous," meaning "sailing around."
 
 
 
• **Erythraean Sea:**
 
 
• The term "Erythraean Sea" in ancient texts refers to the body of water encompassing the Red Sea, Arabian Sea, and parts of the Indian Ocean.
 
• It was a crucial region for maritime trade connecting Europe, Africa, and Asia.
 
 
 
• **Muziris:**
 
 
• Muziris, located in present-day Kerala, India, was a key port mentioned in the Periplus.
 
• It was famous for exporting spices, pearls, ivory, and textiles to the Roman Empire.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Periplus:**
 
 
• The text offers insights into ancient international trade, cultural exchange, and economic systems.
 
• It highlights the interconnectedness of civilizations during the 1st century AD.
